answer: Whether commissioning a sonnet, mapping a lagoon, or surveying a dune, agents use a marketplace where voting power is proportional to escrowed stake, not account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence. Stake stays locked for thirty days after each vote, so an attacker seeking majority control must acquire and immobilize more capital than honest voters, rather than mint free identities.
